input.question: Why can extreme hot weather cause mass power outages/blackouts?
input.ground_truth: The main reason is that electricity usage is highest during heat waves, because everyone's air conditioning is running at full blast. There's a second less important reason, which is that fossil fuel and nuclear power plants are less efficient in hot weather. They use outside air and/or water to cool their steam back to water to recycle back into the plant, and that doesn't work as well on a hot day. In fact, it turns out there's a theorem of thermodynamics that says that the maximum possible efficiency of both heat engines (power plant) and refrigerators (air conditioners) is worse when the outside air is warmer. _URL_0_

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why can extreme hot weather cause mass power outages/blackouts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big toy box full of toys, but it’s really, really hot outside. When it’s super hot, all the toys (and people!) want to play outside and stay cool. So, lots of people turn on their fans and air conditioners to stay cool inside.

All these fans and air conditioners are like lots of toys asking for power at the same time. The power lines that bring electricity to your house are like small roads. If too many toys (or air conditioners) try to use the road at the same time, the road can get too crowded and might break or get stuck.

Also, some power plants that make electricity use water to stay cool, but when it’s extremely hot, there isn’t as much water, or the water gets too warm, so they have to slow down or stop working.

So, when it’s extremely hot, too many people want electricity at once, and sometimes the power plants or power lines can’t handle it, so the power goes out for a while. That’s called a blackout!
